discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: The University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Hidetoshi Katori proposed (2001-2003) trapping neutral atoms in an optical lattice tuned to a 'magic wavelength', where the light shifts of both clock states cancel. Many atoms can then be interrogated at once without perturbing the clock transition, and he demonstrated the first strontium lattice clocks. Jun Ye developed the concept into the most accurate and stable clocks ever built. He advanced ultrastable lasers and the control of many-body interactions, and he reached fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and below. Lattice clocks using Sr, Yb and Hg now outperform the caesium standard by two orders of magnitude and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. They measure gravitational redshift over centimetre height differences and set stringent limits on variations of fundamental constants and on dark matter. This invention created a new precision platform for fundamental physics, and the whole cold-atom community now builds on it.
